title: Hearing arrangements played and instrument weight
summary: On the importance of balancing instruments in arranging, and classical composers having orchestras on hand to try their work.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That’s a long process and I think nowadays of, we write, many of us, on Finale and those programs where you can sort of hear the music as you write it. And I contrast that with years ago when we would write like a big band chart and that moment when it finally gets played and you hear it, and hopefully you hear it in all its glory but in some cases you’re going, “Oh, I didn’t know it was going to sound like that.”

Yes I mean you know as you gain more knowledge of arranging, orchestration, you know, compositions, one comes to realize that one of the most important things is the weight of the instrument against another instrument. And if you, you know, after trial and error should be able to realize that, you know, if you give too much weight on a section it’s going to come out sounding not like what you thought you heard. You know, see the classical musicians from the 1500s on, including Beethoven and all of the greats, Mozart, Haydn, they were lucky. Because all of the musicians were all housed in a barracks at their command every day, so when they scripted out something they brought it over to the barracks, you know, the music area and those guys, you know, played it and they could hear it instantaneously whether it was right or wrong. You know? Think about it.
